item.title: From C.J. Stroud's contract to Texans' 2-5 start, 5 takeaways from Nick Caserio's press conference
item.description: Texans general manager Nick Caserio addressed the media for his only in-season press conference amid the team's disappointing 2-5 start before their off week. (Brett Coomer/Houston Chronicle) The Houston Texans fell to 2-5 on the season after their loss to the New York Giants on Sunday, their worst start in four seasons under coach DeMeco Ryans. And now everything is being questioned heading into their off week. Texans general manager Nick Caserio on Monday held his only in-season press conference ahead of the team's off week, addressing a variety of issues from his own record as a talent evaluator to contract negotiations with C.J. Stroud to why the team has struggled this season. Here are five takeaways from the session: Expectations on Stroud's contract situation The biggest topic of the offseason was whether the Texans would reach an agreement with Stroud's representation on a contract extension. That contract may make him the highest-paid player in NFL history. The Texans and Stroud's agent worked all the way up until the end of the preseason , but did not come to an agreement. Caserio confirmed that the Texans were "pretty close" to a new deal. But when asked if they were close, why not try to get the deal done, the general manager declined to answer. "I don't really have anything else to add," he said. "We negotiated, we went back and forth, we didn't reach an agreement, no hard feelings. Everybody moves forward. I think everybody feels good about where we are, and at some point I would expect an agreement to be figured out." Stroud is outperforming the expectations many had for him. He's playing the best football of his career. He's fourth in the league with 1,877 passing yards, and he has thrown 11 touchdowns to just one interception. "I would say he's gone out there and honestly, he's played really good football, which isn't to the surprise of anybody," Caserio said. "There were very few people other than maybe DeMeco (Ryans) and myself who supported him all offseason when he was essentially bad-mouthed for four months for one bad half of football. I think the way he's handled himself and how he's approached it, speaks to who he is and it's not the surprise of any of us. "I think the contract will take care of itself whenever that is." item.title: La Liga to investigate Camavinga assault during Real Madrid’s Clasico victory
item.description: La Liga to investigate Camavinga assault during Real Madrid’s Clasico victory La Liga is preparing to report an alleged assault on Real Madrid midfielder Eduardo Camavinga during Sunday’s 2-1 victory over Barcelona at the Camp Nou. The incident occurred during celebrations for Kylian Mbappe’s late winning goal, when a supporter appeared to strike Camavinga with a flagpole near the stands. According to The Athletic , footage circulating on social media has prompted La Liga to refer the matter to its Disciplinary Committee. The incident unfolded in the 87th minute after Mbappe scored to secure a crucial victory for Jose Mourinho’s side. Camavinga had played an important role in the goal, advancing past Barcelona defender Pau Cubarsi before providing the pass for his French compatriot to finish. As Madrid’s players celebrated near the home supporters, footage appeared to show an individual swinging a flagpole towards Camavinga. Aurelien Tchouameni intervened during the confrontation, helping move his teammates away from the crowd as tensions escalated. The alleged incident was accompanied by objects being thrown from the stands during the celebrations. Referee Juan Martinez Munuera subsequently documented the disturbances in his official match report. The official recorded that a water bottle and a Coca-Cola can were thrown towards the pitch, although neither object struck a player. The incidents prompted the activation of the stadium’s established protocol for objects being thrown from spectator areas. An announcement was made over the public-address system, while the match was temporarily suspended for one minute and 20 seconds. Although the referee documented the objects thrown, the alleged flagpole incident came to wider attention following the circulation of video footage. La Liga sources have since confirmed to The Athletic that the organisation intends to bring the matter before the relevant disciplinary authorities. The league has reiterated its commitment to tackling violence and intolerance within Spanish football. However, any potential punishment will depend on the disciplinary process and the findings of the authorities responsible for reviewing the evidence. The controversy threatens to overshadow an important result for Real Madrid in the Spanish title race. Mourinho’s team ended Barcelona’s nine-match winning start to the league campaign, inflicting a damaging defeat on their biggest rivals. Mbappe’s late intervention proved decisive after an intensely contested encounter between the two Spanish giants. For Barcelona, the result represented their first domestic setback of the season, while Madrid strengthened their position in the championship race. Attention will now turn to the disciplinary investigation, with La Liga seeking action over the alleged assault and disturbances surrounding the goal celebrations. The outcome could determine whether Barcelona face sanctions for the behaviour of spectators during the high-profile fixture.

item.title: Burnley appoint Chief football officer to facilitate search for new manager
item.description: Burnley appoint Chief football officer to facilitate search for new manager Burnley have confirmed the appointment of Diego Lopez as their new chief football officer to facilitate the search for a new manager after sacking Nicky Hayen. The 37-year-old joins the Clarets from Genoa and will oversee the club’s football operations, player recruitment and long-term sporting plans. His immediate task is to identify a suitable replacement for Hayen, who was sacked after Burnley’s disappointing 4-1 defeat against Lincoln City on Saturday . Rob Edwards is one of several candidates Burnley are considering for the vacant position, although the club has also expanded their search outside England. The 43-year-old is the favourite for the role and has experience managing Wolverhampton Wanderers, Middlesbrough and Luton Town. He also got the latter promoted to the Premier League. Burnley have also been linked with Carlos Corberan, but the former West Bromwich Albion and Valencia manager is reportedly uninterested in taking the job. Corberan left Valencia in September and would prefer taking a job in the Premier League. Despite his relationship with Lopez, he has made it clear he doesn’t want to join Burnley. The Clarets have had a dreadful start to the season. They’ve won just one of their 12 games so far (D5, L6) and sit 22nd in the Championship table. They’ve also failed to win any of their opening six games at Turf Moor (D4, L2), stretching their winless streak at home to more than a year. Chairman Alan Pace appointed Hayen in the summer, hoping the Belgian coach could help the club secure a quick return to the Premier League. Hayen won the Belgian league title with Club Brugge in 2024, but his time at Turf Moor ended after a series of disappointing results. Pace has now brought in Lopez to help rebuild the club and improve its recruitment strategy. “This appointment is about raising standards across the whole football club,” Pace said. “We wanted someone with deep experience in recruitment and player development, a strong knowledge of European markets and a clear understanding of how those come together to strengthen a club over the long term. Diego has a proven record of exactly that.”

item.title: Kylian Mbappe only behind Cristiano Ronaldo as he hits 100-goal milestone for Real Madrid
item.description: Kylian Mbappe only behind Cristiano Ronaldo as he hits 100-goal milestone for Real Madrid Kylian Mbappe reached the 100-goal milestone for Real Madrid in spectacular fashion, scoring twice in the 2-1 victory over Barcelona at Spotify Camp Nou. The French forward needed just 116 appearances to reach his century, becoming the second-fastest player to score 100 goals for the club in the 21st century, behind Cristiano Ronaldo , who achieved the feat in 105 matches. The landmark capped another decisive performance from Mbappe, whose double secured three valuable points for Jose Mourinho’s side while adding another chapter to his increasingly prolific Real Madrid career. Mbappe’s 100 goals for Real Madrid Mbappe’s century for Real Madrid spans six competitions, with La Liga accounting for the largest share of his goals. He has scored 67 goals in La Liga, 25 in the Champions League, four in the Copa del Rey, two in the FIFA Club World Cup, one in the UEFA Super Cup and one in the Spanish Super Cup, completing his century in 116 appearances. His scoring record has remained remarkably consistent since arriving at the Santiago Bernabeu in 2024. Mbappe scored 44 goals in his first season, followed by another 42 during the 2025/26 campaign. He has already registered 14 goals in the current season. Reaching 100 goals in 116 appearances puts him among the most prolific players of Real Madrid’s modern era. Only Cristiano Ronaldo reached the same milestone in fewer matches among the club’s players in the 21st century, highlighting the extraordinary impact Mbappe has made since joining the Spanish giants. Golden Boot, Pichichi and Champions League honours for Mbappe The century is the latest achievement in a remarkable collection of individual honours. Mbappe went on to win the European Golden Shoe in 2024/25, recognising him as Europe’s leading league goalscorer, and claimed the Pichichi Trophy as La Liga’s top scorer in both the 2024/25 and 2025/26 seasons. Prolific. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) He also finished as the leading goalscorer in the 2025/26 Champions League, further establishing himself as one of the most dangerous forwards in European football. His achievements extend to the international stage. Representing France, Mbappe became the highest goalscorer in World Cup history with 22 goals during the 2026 tournament. In 2025, he also matched Cristiano Ronaldo’s Real Madrid record for the most goals scored by a player for the club in a calendar year, finishing with 59. That benchmark, alongside his latest century, illustrates the extraordinary scoring standards Mbappe has maintained across different competitions.

item.title: Daniel Hardy’s Rise Creates A New Puzzle For Bears DC Dennis Allen
item.description: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Daniel Hardy has become a problem for Bears defensive coordinator Dennis Allen, but it is the good kind of problem. This young edge rusher is playing at a level that forces the coaching staff to rethink their entire rotation. The numbers show a clear shift in the defensive front over the last two weeks. Hardy played 51.4 percent of the defensive snaps in the last two games, totaling 56 out of 109 snaps. That is a massive jump from the start of the season when he saw just seven snaps in the first five weeks. He has filled the void left by Montez Sweat’s suspension and Dayo Odeyingbo’s injury with real production. Hardy’s Stats Show Real Impact The statistics from these last two games tell a compelling story about Hardy’s value. Per Bear Goggles On , he has recorded 1.5 sacks, seven total tackles, and one tackle for loss. He also added four quarterback hits and batted down a pass in the backfield. These are not just empty numbers; they show a player who knows how to disrupt the offense. His ability to get to the quarterback is even more impressive when you look at the pass rush data. On 55 pass rush snaps, Hardy generated eight pressures and four quarterback hurries. His pass rush win rate sits at 19.6 percent, which ties for the sixth-best mark among edge rushers this season. That kind of efficiency is rare for a player who was barely on the field until recently. When the defense drops into “true pass sets,” Hardy’s win rate climbs to 26.5 percent, ranking 16th-best in the league. This shows he can handle specific high-leverage situations. He is not just a body on the field; he is getting the job done when it matters most. The Return of the Veterans Now comes the tricky part for Dennis Allen. The team is getting key players back, and Hardy has made it hard to keep him on the bench. Montez Sweat is returning from his two-game suspension. Sweat has not registered a sack in his last two games and has only four combined pressures. Austin Booker currently leads the team with four sacks, tied with Kyler Gordon. The Bears have multiple options, but Hardy’s recent surge complicates the decision. The coaching staff must decide if they keep the hot hand or return to the veterans who have more experience. Allen has to balance the need for immediate production with the long-term plan for the roster. The next game is Monday, Nov. 2, at Seattle Seahawks. The Bears will face a tough pass rush, and every snap counts. If Hardy keeps this up, Allen might have to play both Hardy and the returning stars to get the best pass rush possible.

item.description: Entering Game 3 of the 2026 World Series on Monday, Oct. 16, any Milwaukee Brewers fan paying attention knows the key players. item.title: Kris Dunn is Emerging as an Early Defensive Player of the Year Candidate
item.description: Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic (77) shoots the ball over Los Angeles Clippers guard Kris Dunn (8) during the first quarter at Crypto.com Arena. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Daniel Benjamin, Editor The Los Angeles Clippers have faced tough point guards to start the season. Darius Acuff Jr. and Luka Doncic are both high-volume scorers who use their craft to get to their spots and facilitate at a high level. This level of production is hard to guard against, but not for Kris Dunn . Dunn managed to limit both men during their matchups through the first two games this season, leading to an early candidacy for defensive player of the year for the Los Angeles Clippers’ guard. Locking Up His Matchups Through the First 2 Games The Clippers have played the Sacramento Kings and the Los Angeles Lakers to start this season. The Kings play a high-scoring, volume offense around Acuff Jr., looking to give him all the opportunities he needs to thrive in this league. The Lakers are led by Doncic, one of the NBA’s premier offensive talents. Both men are tough covers who can do it all on offense, from shooting and scoring to facilitating. Dunn has been tasked with matching up against the opposing team’s best offensive guards to limit their production. Relieving Darius Garland from His Defensive Duties Los Angeles Clippers guard Darius Garland (10) goes up for a basket beside Oklahoma City Thunder center Chet Holmgren (7) during the second half at Paycom Center. Photo Credit: Alonzo Adams-Imagn Images Darius Garland is the starting point guard for the Los Angeles Clippers. Given Garland’s heavy offensive workload and defensive struggles, having him guard the opposing team’s primary ball handler is not an easy ask. Dunn has emerged to relieve Garland of his defensive duties by covering the opposing team’s point guards himself. Giving Darius Acuff Jr. a Debut to Forget The 2026 NBA draft was projected to be one of the greatest in NBA history. Acuff Jr. was one of the names mentioned among the top talent in the class, with his elite offensive ability a notable skill set. The Kings have said they will allow Acuff Jr. to shoot at a high volume to unlock his full potential as a rookie. This showed in his debut game as Acuff Jr. shot the ball 24 times. Acuff Jr. quickly learned that scoring on Dunn is no easy task, as the rookie made only 5 of his 24 shots. Dunn also restricted Acuff from making the right reads by getting his hands in passing lanes and forcing passes out of uncomfortable dribbles. This forced Acuff Jr. to record only three assists against four turnovers, further limiting his impact on the defensive end. The credit does not completely go to Dunn, as he did not cover the rookie in every possession. However, the Kings did shoot only 2-for-9 when the Clippers guard was the primary defender. item.title: Seattle sports fans turn to transit as Sound Transit sees ridership jump
item.description: Sound Transit With Seahawks, Kraken, and Sounders games in full swing, Seattle sports fans have more ways to get to the stadiums, and Sound Transit says more people are taking advantage of public transportation on game days. After last year’s Super Bowl win, Seahawks fans are flocking to home games hoping the team can do it again this year. For fans living on the Eastside, there is now another option for getting to the stadium with the new crosslake connection. Sound Transit’s David Jackson said ridership at Eastside stations is more than 100% higher on Sundays with games compared with Sundays without games. “People are coming early. They’re taking advantage of the train,” Jackson said. On opening night of the Seahawks season, Sound Transit said nearly 5,000 riders used South Bellevue Station, a 53% increase over the previous week’s baseline. That game was played on a Wednesday. Jackson said fans can also avoid some of the costs that come with driving to a game. “They’re not driving, they’re not spending $5 a gallon in gas, and they’re paying for parking,” Jackson said, adding that a trip costs $3 each way. The increased game-day use isn’t limited to Link light rail. Sound Transit has added an extra Sounder train from both the Tacoma-Lakewood and Everett corridors this season. The agency said more than 3,000 passengers are using Sounder for Sunday daytime games. And football isn’t the only sport driving demand. Jackson said crowds can also be seen at Westlake during Kraken games, where riders can transfer to the monorail. Sounders games are also popular with transit riders, he said. For fans planning to use transit for an upcoming game, Sound Transit recommends getting to the light rail station early if they plan to use a park-and-ride before it fills up.

item.title: Mike Vrabel gives updates on injured Patriots, including Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown
item.description: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - OCTOBER 18: Ben Brown #77 and Alijah Vera-Tucker #75 of the New England Patriots walk out of the tunnel before the game against the New York Jets at Gillette Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots were back to work Monday following a weekend off. Ahead of a bonus practice day, head coach Mike Vrabel provided updates on several injured players. That began along the offensive line. After being placed on injured reserve Thursday with a hamstring injury, Alijah Vera-Tucker is expected to return at some point this season. “I don’t think it’s for the season, but I couldn’t tell you what short term is determined by, you know, however many weeks he has to be out,” Vrabel said. “But, it wasn’t going to be this week, so we figured it was going to be at least four games. So, that’s why we made the decision that we made.” The Patriots did get some positive injury news along the offensive line, as fellow guard Ben Brown returned to practice on Monday. Brown missed last week’s game with a knee injury he suffered agains the Jets. Vrabel also noted that the team will have to make a decision on offensive tackle Marcus Bryant, whose 21-day activation window from injured reserve closes this week. Meanwhile, offensive guard Greg Van Roten and safety Dell Pettus could return to practice this week as they work their way back from injured reserve. The Patriots will continue managing their injured reserve list for the rest of the season, with just six return designations remaining. “The depth that you have at the position or the need and I don’t think it’s something that you really want to make a habit of but we’re in the position that we are,” Vrabel said of managing it. “So kind of figuring out, one who’s healthy. who’s healthy enough to return. Some guys aren’t and then we’ll see where we go with the depth at each position.” On the practice field Monday, the Patriots managed the workload of several veterans as they were without Rhamondre Stevenson, Marcus Jones, Dre’Mont Jones, Christian Elliss, Robert Spillane, Kevin Byard, Hunter Henry and Morgan Moses.

item.title: Mikal Bridges’ Knicks Disaster Leaves Nets Fans Bitter
item.description: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images The trade that sent Mikal Bridges to New York for six first-round picks looked like a massive overpay from the start. Now, with the Knicks sitting at 0-3 and Bridges shooting just 5-of-23 from the field, the deal looks even worse. The player is averaging only 3.3 points per game while recording a negative plus-minus in every contest. It is a total disaster for the franchise that gave up so much to get him. A Wake-Up Call for the Defending Champs New York looks nothing like the juggernaut that won the NBA title less than four months ago. The team allowed Orlando to score 40 points in a single quarter, a collapse that no champion should accept. Legendary commentator Mike Breen called the slow start a “wake-up call” during the game against the Magic on Sunday. Even Jalen Brunson, the Finals MVP, is shooting just 39% from the field and has admitted that “everything falls on my shoulders.” The defense is broken, and the stars are missing their shots. Coach Mike Brown has been blunt about the reality facing his squad. He told his players that “our crap stinks” and that they are the only ones who can fix it. Brown broke the season into five-game segments to track progress, noting that “if you’re doing anything less than that, you know that nobody is reaching their potential.” The Knicks have not reached their potential in the first three games, and the margin for error is now razor-thin. Brooklyn Fans Have No Joy to Share You would think the Brooklyn Nets fans would be laughing at their crosstown rivals after such a bad start. Because the Nets hold the rights to this season’s Knicks first-round pick, they ought to celebrate the trade’s failure. Instead, they are stuck in their own misery because the Nets are also 0-3. They lost their opener to a Charlotte team without key players and got blown out in Cleveland. According to FanSided , currently only the Nets could be a greater disaster than the Knicks. Brooklyn lost their third game by 27 points at home, proving they have their own severe problems. The trade was supposed to build a contender for New York and a foundation for Brooklyn, but it has resulted in two terrible teams. The six picks might be worth something someday, but right now they just sit in a pocket while both teams lose. The Long Road Ahead Three games out of 82 mean very little in the grand scheme of things, but the trend is scary. Since the Dallas Mavericks achieved this in the shortened 2011-12 season, the Knicks remain the sole defending champions beginning a season 0-3. That Dallas team finished 36-30 and got swept in the first round. New York cannot afford to follow that path. The next game is against the unbeaten Detroit Pistons, which will be an extremely physical matchup. item.title: Liverpool set to lose crucial pair just one year in to Andoni Iraola's reign
item.description: Liverpool set to lose crucial pair just one year in to Andoni Iraola's reign Liverpool's start to life under Andoni Iraola has been difficult to judge. The Reds have dominated some games, recording some very convincing victories, but Iraola's side have also faced some crushing defeats. Inconsistency across the pitch has been a big problem for the Spaniard to deal with, but injuries have also limited the team early on. It is clear that there is still plenty of work to be done before this squad is ready to compete at the very top again, but two of the Reds' most important players are reportedly nearing the exit door. The Anfield recruitment team will already be working on replacements, but this double loss would be a huge blow to Iraola. Liverpool preparing for double exit in the summer One of Julian Ward's first problems in his new role as Liverpool's sporting director is the array of expiring contracts he is faced with. Seven members of the first-team squad are currently on track to leave for free at the end of the 2026/27 season. Alisson, Virgil van Dijk , Joe Gomez , Kostas Tsimikas, Wataru Endo, Luke Chambers and Harvey Davies are all into the final 12 months of their current deals and, whilst some extensions will no doubt be negotiated, two stars are reportedly set to leave Anfield. That's according to a report from Football Insider , which claims that both Van Dijk and Gomez are expected to leave for free in the summer upon the expiry of their contracts. The loss of Van Dijk, who has played every minute of the Premier League campaign so far, is in itself a massive blow to the Reds, but to lose Gomez as well could cripple Iraola's defence. The Englishman has been a massive asset for Liverpool in recent years because of his experience and ability to play multiple positions across the backline. A very capable defender in his own right, Gomez has a lot to offer at Anfield when he is fit, but the problem for several seasons has been trying to keep the 29-year-old out of the treatment room. The 15-capped England international has played just over 100 minutes under Iraola after missing the start of the season with a muscle injury. Van Dijk's age, 35, is the big barrier when it comes to renewing the skipper. The Dutchman is still performing at an extremely high level though, and to lose one of let alone both of Van Dijk and Gomez would be a massive blow to Liverpool.

item.title: Dez Bryant’s Gunpoint Claim Sparks Outrage Among Cowboys Fans
item.description: Alonzo Adams-USA TODAY Sports Dez Bryant says a police officer pointed a gun at him. This happened on Sunday in Southlake, Texas, during a traffic dispute. The former Cowboys star claims the situation was handled poorly from the start. He says he felt the officer took the other side without doing the proper work. Bryant told Fox News’ Outkick that the trouble began with reckless drivers. He alleges two men cut him off and put him in a dangerous spot. Bryant claims he told them to drive safer. The argument escalated until one man threatened to pull a firearm. “He go to threatening me and basically saying, um, he’ll insinuate that he’ll, you know, he’ll shoot me or whatever,” Bryant said, according to BroBible . Footage Shows A Gun Aimed At A Legend Video released to the public shows the officer aiming his weapon directly at Bryant. The footage also shows Bryant lying on the ground in handcuffs. He was not the only one restrained that day. “Footage provided to OutKick by Bryant showed an officer aiming a gun in Bryant’s direction. Bryant is also seen lying on the ground in handcuffs alongside the two other men in Southlake, Texas,” Outkick reported. The presence of his children made this moment even harder to bear. Bryant says his main worry was not the gun itself, but his kids seeing their father treated this way. “I was really more so concerned about my children, you know, looking at their dad, you know, being on the ground with a gun pointed at me,” Bryant said, according to Yahoo Sports . No one was hurt, but the emotional toll on the family is clear. The Citation And The Court Date Despite claiming he was the one threatened, Bryant received an assault citation. During the dispute, he struck a phone from one man’s hand. Now he faces a court date in Southlake. Bryant is scheduled to appear at Southlake Municipal Court on or before Nov. 20 at 5 p.m. He thinks the police ought to have brought everyone to the station for a genuine investigation. Instead, they let the other men go while citing him. “I would rather you guys take us all down to the police station and do the proper investigation instead of just taking somebody else, you know, side,” Bryant said. He feels the whole encounter was very one-sided and unfair to him. As the Cowboys prepare for Monday night against the Eagles, this story dominates the local talk. The team has struggled on offense recently, but this legal battle for their former star is a different kind of fight. Bryant says he usually has good ties with local police, including an officer who coaches his son’s high school team. “Every time I see him, we talk ball. We just talk about the regular things,” Bryant said of that officer. “It’s always been good. This situation was just extremely unfortunate.”

item.title: Mason Kucenski living a dream as Red Wings' emergency goaltender
item.description: DETROIT — There are still plenty of days when Mason Kucenski looks around the Red Wings locker room, takes notice of players he used to watch on television or read about, and all of this doesn't seem real. Kucenski is the Red Wings' emergency backup goaltender (EBUG). All 32 teams are now required to have one in the new collective bargaining agreement, a goaltender with no previous NHL game experience (and fewer than 80 games pro experience total), but who is there at practice every day, both home and away. The job may not be for everybody, but for Kucenski it's a dream come true. He's living the life of an NHL player, basically, though he's not on the roster and likely will never get to play in a game. It doesn't matter. Kucenski is there in the locker room. He's on the ice, with the Wings, facing their shots. He's on the team plane, on the bus. It's a unique experience Kucenski is relishing and enjoying every moment, he can. "A great experience so far," said Kucenski, 24, who played collegiately at St. Lawrence (New York) from 2023-26. "It's a lifetime goal of mine to be in the NHL. It's all just surreal." Kucenski has played hockey since he was about 5 years old, and it was right from the start that he knew he wanted to be a goaltender. "I just fell in love with it right away," Kucenski said. More: Red Wings' Michal Postava to get first NHL start Monday against Edmonton The NHL was obviously the dream, but Kucenski was never drafted and the hockey dream looked crushed once his senior season at St. Lawrence ended. But Kucenski received a call from Brian Daccord, the Wings' director of goaltending and scouting development, early in the summer, and the dream suddenly was revitalized. The NHL wanted to get away from the old system of amateurs supplied from the local area, who maybe had some pro experience, and could play if both goaltenders on a team's roster suddenly were hurt, or sick, or unavailable to play for some reason. Now, the team's EBUG isn't officially on the roster but he's part of the team, being there every day. "It was a quick yes from me," said Kucenski, a native of Gill, Massachusetts, after Daccord explained what the role would entail and if Kucenski would be interested. "It kind of just rolled on from there." Kucenski also interviewed with Michael Leighton, the Wings' goaltending coach, and Dwayne Blais, the player development consultant, and the fit, from everybody's angle, was perfect. Understandably, there was some uneasiness from Kucenski walking into the Wings' locker room, not knowing how he'd be received, not knowing anyone, and just the uncertainty of the position. But Kucenski was accepted as a part of the team from the first practice. " All the guys have been great to me so far and they've all taken me in," Kucenski said. "They've really been nice to me, showing me how to navigate the NHL." item.title: Steelers’ Mike McCarthy praises jumbo package, OL Spencer Anderson
item.description: Photo By Winslow Townson/Getty Images | Getty Images In a callback to the Steelers’ 2025 offense under Arthur Smith, Pittsburgh broke out its six-offensive-lineman package versus the Saints on Sunday. And in a 16-10 win where the Steelers out-rushed New Orleans 148 yards to 18, it’s fair to say the decision paid off. Like last year, utility offensive lineman Spencer Anderson served as the extra blocker in the jumbo package, playing 13 snaps on Sunday. Twelve of those were run plays, and per Steelers writer Tom Mead , the results on those rushes were 77 yards, 6.4 yards per carry and three runs over nine or more yards. Speaking to the media on Monday, Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said the Steelers’ jumbo package success in 2025 “absolutely” played a role in its return in 2026. “When you get the job, the first thing you do, you sit and down and starting going through the personnel,” McCarthy said. “And Spencer (Anderson), I was so impressed with him and it was a big part of the discussion of how we were trying to forecast him for where we felt he could play, because he played so many positions.” McCarthy compared Anderson to current Bills and former Cowboys lineman Conner McGovern, saying he can play every role from center to guard to fullback: “We gotta get him on the field,” McCarthy said. “When you have someone like Spencer with his unique talents, it gives you such great versatility,” he added. McCarthy hinted that part of why the jumbo package didn’t play a major role in the Steelers’ game plan until Week 7 was because the Steelers first gave Anderson the starting right guard role to open the season. Then, Anderson dealt with a bone chip in his right leg in late September. “In fairness to (Anderson), I wanted to give him a chance to compete for a job, and that’s why we started the way we did with him at right guard, and then he had the injury and so forth,” McCarthy said. Despite free agent signing Brock Hoffman having secured the starting right guard spot moving forward, McCarthy indicated that the Steelers still want to find ways to get Anderson on the field. “(Anderson) carries a lot of value on our football team, especially up front,” the Pittsburgh head coach said, “and it’s important for us to continue to create opportunities for him.”
